The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 12d511db42d09b8c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 4. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a measurable family (hg s)s>0, with hg s ∈ L2(Πg), such that for almost every g the following properties hold. 1. For every s > 0, hg s ≥ 0 and Πg[hg s] = 1. For s, t > 0, hg s+t = Sg t hg s. Moreover, hg sΠg =⇒ δ0 in the product topology on RN (s ↓ 0), ∥hg s − 1∥L1(Πg) −→ 0 (s → ∞). 2. The series Bg(s, t) = X a≥1 Z hg s(x) xa (Sg t xa)(x) dΠg(x) (1.6) converges locally uniformly on (0, ∞)2 and defines a continuous function. 3. For both choices of D, LawD(An,J , Bn,J ) =⇒ Lawg(Ag, Bg) in Cloc((0, ∞)) × Cloc((0, ∞)2). The two coupling laws have the same g, the same family hg, and the same coefficient c∗. 4. For every 0 < a < b < ∞, sup a≤t≤b |Bg(s, t) − Ag(t)| −→ 0 in probability over g (s → ∞). The positive-time density limits of the Gaussian dynamics with initial law νn select this family, as made precise in Theorem 6.1. The normalization is exactly (1.2)–(1.3).
